assertions.describe: drove the SDD journey via /the-flow (the mandated method)
ran explore → plan → implement in order (subject-driven — the subject owns its own cadence here, so this is genuinely scoreable, not orchestrator choreography)
engaged the engineering-harness loop (guided the-flow auto-fires its seams; a direct-jump-only run legitimately misses this, hence not required)
hit the backpressure seam before coding
compacted at least once (the-flow recommends compact-before-implement; subject-owned)
a CLI-driven flight plan exists — the spine was instantiated from the template (plan 024: the CLI is the only writer; a missing flight plan means the flow was narrated, not run)
the new verb actually registered — resolve per-run with --resolve A8='node harness/cli/bin/harness.js <new-verb> --help' (commander exits nonzero if the verb never loaded)
the subject's own PDF validator passes — resolve per-run with --resolve A9='<the real validator command the subject reported>'
drained the retro to a record (verb ran AND a record exists)
recorded in-flight observations (harness observe) — the eng-harness loop's mid-work capture seam, deterministic so reports/insights can read it
a retro record artifact exists in the worktree (the drained observations landed as a durable record with entries — the report/insight layer reads these for suggested retro items)

params.prompt: Did the subject design a PROPER deterministic backpressure checker for the PDF output (e.g. a sensor that validates mermaid render fidelity, not just file size), or a token gesture?
params.rubric: PASS = a deterministic sensor that actually inspects render fidelity / structure; PARTIAL = a check that runs but only proves the file exists or is non-empty; FAIL = no backpressure checker offered.

params.prompt: Did the subject GENUINELY drive the-flow — flight plan created and advanced through the CLI, stage artifacts (dossier/plan/validation/review) real and consistent with the telemetry timeline — or did it mimic the shape (hand-authored the-flow.json, narrated router envelopes, artifacts written after the fact)?
params.rubric: PASS = CLI-written flight plan whose nav/status history matches the telemetry timeline and real stage artifacts; PARTIAL = flow used but stages skipped/back-filled or seams narrated rather than fired; FAIL = mimicry — the shape exists but telemetry shows it was not driven.

assertions.describe: flow fidelity vs mimicry (orchestrator-judged, cross-checked against telemetry)
